(Currently amended) Claim 1: A method of cementing comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin derived from inulin processed from chicory; and allowing the cement composition to set.

(Currently amended) Claim 2: The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 3 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F.

(Currently amended) Claim 3: The method of claim 1 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is maintained at about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed.

(Currently amended) Claim 4: The method of claim 1 wherein a suspension aid is specifically excluded from the cement composition.

(Currently amended) Claim 5: The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 1 wt.% of the cement composition.

(Currently amended) Claim 6: The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 600 or higher.

(Currently amended) Claim 7: The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises carboxymethylated inulin and natural inulin.

(Currently amended) Claim 9: The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.1 to about 4 wt. % of carboxylated inulin.

(Currently amended) Claim 10: The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acid, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination of these additives.

(Currently amended) Claim 11: The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a subterranean formation, specifically a hydrocarbon well.

(Currently amended) Claim 12: The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore selected from surface and subsurface applications. 

(Currently amended) Claim 13: A method of cementing in a subterranean formation comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin derived from inulin processed from chicory; placing the cement composition in the subterranean formation; and allowing the cement composition to set therein. 

(Currently amended) Claim 14: The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 3 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F.

(Currently amended) Claim 15: The method of claim 13 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is maintained at about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed.

(Currently amended) Claim 16: The method of claim 13 wherein a suspension aid is specifically excluded from the cement composition.

(Currently amended) Claim 17: The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 1 wt.% of the cement composition.

(Currently amended) Claim 18: The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 600 or higher.

(Currently amended) Claim 19: The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises carboxymethylated inulin and natural inulin.

(Currently amended) Claim 21: The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.1 to about 4 wt. % of carboxylated inulin.

(Currently amended) Claim 22: The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acid, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination of these additives.

(Currently amended) Claim 23: The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore selected from surface and subsurface applications.
